lead.headline: TWO FOREIGN VISITORS DIE IN SUSPECTED HOTEL POOL ELECTROCUTION
lead.deck: An American guest and a hotel employee were also hurt in the rescue; investigators are examining a suspected electrical leak
paragraphs: A German and a Slovakian national died after a suspected electric leak in the swimming pool at Bengaluru’s Conrad Hotel on Friday night, police said. An American guest and a hotel employee were injured while trying to rescue them and were taken to hospital.

Police have registered a case. The electrical inspectorate is investigating how current entered the pool; preliminary findings reported by The Times of India suggest the suspected shock was confined to a small area near the pool ladder.
The hotel closed the pool for maintenance after the incident. Officials have not yet announced a final cause.

sidebarStory.headline: BENGALURU–MUMBAI VANDE BHARAT SLEEPER TO DEPART TODAY
sidebarStory.subhead: Inaugural run leaves SMVT Bengaluru at 12:15 pm; regular service begins November 3
paragraphs: The inaugural special is scheduled to leave Sir M Visvesvaraya Terminal Bengaluru at 12:15 pm and reach Mumbai’s CSMT at 6:15 am Monday. Regular sleeper services are due to begin November 3, with eight intermediate stops.

stories.headline: NEW VANDE BHARAT TO LINK BENGALURU AND GOA VIA MANGALURU
stories.deck: The approved route will run through Hassan and coastal Karnataka
paragraphs: The Railway Board has approved a Yesvantpur–Madgaon Vande Bharat service via Hassan and Mangaluru. The planned route includes Udupi, Kundapura, Murdeshwar, Gokarna Road and Karwar; reports put the journey at about 13 hours 20 minutes.

stories.headline: DROPPED TOKEN TRIGGERS 18-MINUTE METRO DISRUPTION
paragraphs: A passenger entered the tracks at Indiranagar station to retrieve a dropped token, prompting emergency systems to stop trains. Normal service resumed about 18 minutes later, BMRCL said; police said the man was working in the city.

stories.headline: BENGALURU–GOA RAIL LINK APPROVED FOR SIX DAYS A WEEK
paragraphs: The proposed Yesvantpur–Madgaon service is planned to operate six days a week, excluding Wednesday. It follows approval of a new Vande Bharat route connecting Bengaluru with Goa through coastal Karnataka.

stories.headline: ASHUTOSH DIXIT TAKES CHARGE AS AIR CHIEF
stories.deck: The Air Chief Marshal assumed office on Saturday, succeeding A. P. Singh
paragraphs: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit assumed charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on October 31, the Defence Ministry said. He succeeds Air Chief Marshal A. P. Singh.
Dixit is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy and was commissioned into the Indian Air Force’s fighter stream in 1986.

stories.headline: NILEKANI-LED EXAM REFORMS PANEL GETS EXTENSION TO JANUARY
paragraphs: The Centre has extended the examination-reforms task force chaired by Nandan Nilekani until January 2027. The panel is reviewing changes to public examinations, including a possible hybrid NEET-UG format, and is consulting states on testing infrastructure and preparedness.

stories.headline: DELHI LOGS COLDEST OCTOBER DAY IN 75 YEARS
paragraphs: The maximum temperature at Safdarjung fell to 20.7°C on Friday, the lowest October day reading there since 1951, after persistent rain. Delhi also recorded its wettest October in four years, according to reports citing the India Meteorological Department.

stories.headline: NANDINI MILK PRICE RISE TAKES EFFECT ACROSS KARNATAKA
stories.deck: The revised base price rises from ₹46 to ₹54 per litre
paragraphs: The ₹8-per-litre increase in Nandini milk prices takes effect today. The revised base price for a litre rises from ₹46 to ₹54; the state says the change is intended to raise payments to dairy farmers.
The Karnataka Milk Federation has also revised curd prices. Consumers should check the rate printed on the packet for the specific product and pack size.

stories.headline: STATE CLOSES 12 PACKAGED-WATER UNITS AFTER INSPECTIONS
paragraphs: Food-safety officials inspected 102 packaged-water units in a two-day statewide drive and shut 12 over issues including unhygienic premises and licensing violations. Two of the closed units were in Bengaluru Urban and one in Bengaluru Rural, according to the report.

stories.headline: E-KHATA CAMPS DISPOSE OF 618 APPLICATIONS AT 62 CENTRES
paragraphs: Greater Bengaluru Authority camps across 62 centres in the five city corporations disposed of 618 e-Khata applications on Saturday, including cases received earlier, the authority reported.

stories.headline: INDIA BEATS JAPAN 4–1, BOOKS ASIAN CHAMPIONS TROPHY SEMIFINAL
stories.deck: Abhishek’s brace helped the defending champions reach the last four with a perfect group record
paragraphs: Abhishek scored twice as India defeated Japan 4–1 in Jalandhar on Friday, securing a semifinal place at the Hero Asian Champions Trophy. Harmanpreet Singh and Vishnu Kant also scored as India made it three wins from three.
India faces Malaysia today in its next group match.

stories.headline: INDIA MEETS MALAYSIA IN JALANDHAR TODAY
paragraphs: India’s men play Malaysia in the Asian Champions Trophy group stage today after both teams secured semifinal places. India qualified with a 4–1 win over Japan, its third successive victory.
